note: G2 duel plan. The pre-registered rule below was written before any live game; change it only by a new version, never after a result. Thresholds marked captainToConfirm are proposed defaults.

policies.note: Every seat plays Greedy through the Jev orchestrator. The treatment arm seats Hard at the focal seat and Normal at every other seat; the control arm seats Normal everywhere. Nothing else differs: same seed, classes, Starters and personality.

design.unit: block = one seed with one focal seat
design.blocksPerSeed: one per seat: Hard sits in every seat for every seed, so a seat or class advantage cancels
design.order: seed ascending, then focal seat, then control before treatment, so an interrupted run leaves whole pairs
design.dependence: A block's two arms share a seed but not their dice after the first different decision. The two blocks of one seed have the same control configuration (Normal on both seats, same seed, classes and Starters), and the control game is played again for each block. On a deterministic client the two control games are the same game; live, Jev's answers differ between plays, so they are the same start and a different course. The analysis resamples blocks as if independent, which is not exactly true: when the two control games agree, the two blocks of a seed share their control score and the stated interval can be too narrow. The report therefore also prints the same difference with whole seeds resampled (a sensitivity, not part of the rule), so the reader can see how much it moves.
design.analysis: sim/analysis/paired.ts (analyzePaired): per-block score difference, Hard minus Normal, with a stratified percentile bootstrap over blocks within (seat count, focal seat) cells.
design.realism: The sim does not send Sell Phase questions (no Sell facts yet, ai/README.md), so those decisions use the fallback on both difficulties. Hard's rollouts act only on Strategy and Encounter, so the duel covers every decision where Hard differs from Normal.

seeds.note: A multiple of 6 seeds, so every class takes every seat equally often. Run a prefix by --seeds only for a smaller n chosen before the run.

seedLedger.role: G2 evaluation seeds. Disjoint from every range in sim/experiments/c5-plan.json; never tuned on. The live run is the first and only use.

power.metric: score difference per block (Hard minus Normal)
power.sdNote: Two independent games, each a win-or-lose score with variance about 0.25 at two seats (0.25 + 0.25 = 0.5, SD 0.7071). A correlation between the arms, shared by the seed, would lower it; none is assumed. The two blocks of a seed share their control configuration, so the SD of a seed's mean difference can be larger than this; the seed-cluster sensitivity in the report shows it.
power.captainToConfirm: The smallest gap worth a third level is a product call. 0.10 means Hard scores 0.60 against Normal's 0.50 at a two-seat table: about 60 games in 100 won, not 50.

cost.inputTokensSource: docs/jev-spike-report.md: mean input tokens per request over the 26 Oct live pair; SPEND_CONFIG.estimatedInputTokensPerRequest is 3,240
cost.requestsSource: mean of 24 offline games (6 seeds x 2 seats x 2 arms) on the seeded fake client, 589 requests, see docs/experiments/g2-hard-vs-normal.md; not a live number: the live run measures it in logs/jev-usage.jsonl

rule.writtenBefore: any live game of this plan

integrity.jevAnsweredNote: Plan v2. Jev answered = of the decisions sent to Jev, the share where Jev returned a valid answer, for Hard and for Normal each: applied (no fallback) or below the confidence threshold (low_confidence, where Jev answered validly and the fallback decided). The denominator is every counted decision (not auto) less missing_facts, which never reached Jev (the Sell Phase questions the sim never asks, and facts a question needs). invalid_choice, schema_mismatch, revision_mismatch, request_limit, token_budget, budget_exceeded and the infrastructure causes stay in the denominator and out of the numerator. Fallbacks that are Jev's own judgement (low_confidence, invalid_choice, revision_mismatch) and missing_facts stay out of the infrastructure share. Hard's own timeouts are not counted in Hard's infrastructure share: Hard's rollouts spend part of the deadline, so Hard's timeout excess over Normal's is the latency rule's job (latency-timeouts); Normal has no rollout, so all its listed causes count. Spend-guard fallbacks (budget_exceeded) are held at zero above. A dead service, a refused key or a run of timeouts fails these checks, so an outage can never be read as 'Hard is no better'.
integrity.captainToConfirm: maxInfrastructureFallbackShare (0.05). minJevAnsweredShare was 0.30 in v1 (decisions with no fallback over all decisions not auto) and is 0.80 in v2: see docs/experiments/g2-hard-vs-normal.md, Plan v2. The smoke run on tuning seeds 100200-100205 showed v1 counted our own low_confidence fallback and the Sell decisions the sim never sends (hard 0.364 of 165, normal 0.244 of 464).
integrity.onFailure: no verdict: fix the cause and play the plan again on fresh seeds

evidence.captainToConfirm: minPointEstimate: Hard must be ahead with a 95% interval that excludes zero, and by at least half the 0.10 gap the run is sized for.

latency.basis: Spec §5.6: a decision returns by 1,500 ms and Hard's rollouts take at most 400 ms of it. Spec §1: AI decision time per turn p95 at most 2 s. Hard's share of decisions that fall back on a timeout may exceed Normal's by at most 0.02.

verdict.keepThreeLevels: integrity holds AND evidence holds AND latency holds
verdict.shipTwoLevels: integrity holds and either evidence or latency fails: Easy and Normal ship, Hard is cut (spec §10 'Cut if late: Monte Carlo'), and the report says which part failed
verdict.noVerdict: an integrity check fails, or planned blocks are missing: say so, never read a partial run as G2
verdict.neverDo: Do not add hidden information, change what Hard's rollouts read or tune the rollout defaults after seeing a result to move the verdict (spec §8).
